submission.justification: Absorber-F1 with 5 mm plate thickness provides the best energy resolution at 100 GeV (3.132%), which is approximately 18% better than F3 (3.836%) and 35% better than F2 (4.794%). Systematic simulations across the allowed thickness range (2-10 mm) confirmed that 5 mm is optimal for all materials, with resolution degrading for both thinner and thicker plates. F1's superior performance stems from its dense alloy composition with short radiation length, enabling better electromagnetic shower sampling. All candidate materials are mechanically compatible with the support structure and cooling system. The residual dose rate constraint must be verified through activation calculations or measurements, but all three materials are presented as viable candidates, suggesting pre-screening for safety requirements.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the best possible energy resolution at 100 GeV
requirements.evidence: Absorber-F1 at 5mm achieves 3.132% resolution, the best among all tested configurations. Simulations tested thicknesses from 2-7mm for all materials.

requirements.requirement: Absorber must be one of three materials in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Absorber-F1 is listed in candidate_specs.md as a dense alloy with short radiation length.

requirements.requirement: Residual dose rate at 1m after one week cooldown must not exceed 20 uSv/h
